boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten campus places with documented uses for studying, relaxing, gathering, recreation, or connecting with faculty and classmates.

cards.title: Reset Between Classes in the Commuter Lounge
cards.subtitle: A commuter-only room in Baugher Student Center 246
cards.notes: Bring your College ID for entry, reserve a locker through Commuter Engagement, and use the refrigerator or microwave between classes.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated home base where commuting students can store belongings, prepare food, study, and pause between campus commitments.
cards.evidence_claim: Elizabethtown College identifies the Commuter Lounge in BSC 246 as a commuter-only space with ID-card access, lockers, a refrigerator, microwave, and Keurig.
cards.access_notes: Reserved for commuters; entry requires an Elizabethtown College ID card. Locker reservations are handled through commuter@etown.edu.

cards.title: Find a Quiet Reset at The Well
cards.subtitle: Relaxation and study space on the Bowers Center’s second floor
cards.notes: Use the quiet seating for a short study break, or reserve the Relaxation Room’s Sleep Pod for one 20-minute session through Bowers Center.
cards.short_summary: A wellness-oriented pause point combining quiet study space with a reservable relaxation room inside the recreation center.
cards.evidence_claim: The College says The Well has a quiet relaxation and study space on the Bowers Center’s second floor, including a Sleep Pod reservable for 20 minutes.
cards.access_notes: The Bowers Center limits access to students, employees, Family Rec Pass users, and Affiliate Members with valid identification; visitors require an escort.

cards.title: Switch From Study Mode to Table Games
cards.subtitle: A common room inside Baugher Student Center
cards.notes: Settle in for individual work, then use the pool or ping-pong table when you need a screen break; lockers can be reserved through Commuter Engagement.
cards.short_summary: A student-center common room where quiet work and low-key recreation share the same space.
cards.evidence_claim: Elizabethtown College describes the Bird Cage as a Baugher Student Center common room for relaxing and studying, equipped with pool, ping-pong, and television.
cards.access_notes: Inside Baugher Student Center. College building access is restricted to students, employees, and invited guests or visitors.

cards.title: Match the Library Floor to the Work
cards.subtitle: Flexible study and research space at the High Library
cards.notes: Use the first floor when conversation helps, or reserve a study room online or at a library kiosk when your group needs a defined workspace.
cards.short_summary: The first floor supports less-quiet work, while reservable rooms give groups a dedicated place to collaborate.
cards.evidence_claim: The College identifies High Library’s first floor as a research and work space that is not designated quiet, and says students may reserve study rooms by time slot.
cards.access_notes: Study-room reservations are first come, first served; unreserved rooms may be used on a drop-in basis. Check the library website for current building hours.

cards.title: Use a Dedicated Study Stop in Brossman Commons
cards.subtitle: Second-floor workspace in Brossman Commons
cards.notes: Head to the second floor when you want a purpose-built study space near the Commons instead of settling into a dining or recreation area.
cards.short_summary: A clearly designated study area positioned on the second floor of Brossman Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: Elizabethtown College lists the Learning Zone as a dedicated study space on the second floor of Brossman Commons.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Brossman Commons. College building access is restricted to students, employees, and invited guests or visitors.

cards.title: Take Group Activities Onto Brinser Field
cards.subtitle: A central lawn beside Wolf Field and Brossman Commons
cards.notes: Use the open grass for casual outdoor activity, but contact Facilities Management before planning an organized event or requesting field features.
cards.short_summary: A large, centrally located lawn that can accommodate different outdoor activities and formal campus events.
cards.evidence_claim: The College describes Brinser Field as a large grassy field beside Wolf Field and Brossman Commons that is suitable for multiple outdoor activities.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space is generally open to the public, but the College may restrict access. Organized use may require Facilities Management permission.

cards.title: Move a Study Session Into the Academic Quad
cards.subtitle: The central green beside Brossman Commons
cards.notes: Claim a picnic table near Thompson Gymnasium or an Adirondack chair near Esbenshade Hall when weather makes outdoor reading practical.
cards.short_summary: A central campus lawn with two documented seating options for studying or meeting outside.
cards.evidence_claim: Elizabethtown College describes the Academic Quad as a central grassy area beside Brossman Commons with picnic tables and nearby Adirondack study chairs.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space is generally open to the public, but Elizabethtown College may restrict access at any time.

cards.title: Study Beside the Mineral Collection
cards.subtitle: Gallery and atrium seating inside the Masters Center
cards.notes: Bring work to the tables or lounge chairs near the gallery, then examine the labeled mineral displays during a short break from studying.
cards.short_summary: A weekday public gallery whose adjoining atrium also provides tables and lounge seating used for studying.
cards.evidence_claim: The College says the Masters Mineral Gallery and adjacent atrium provide tables and lounge chairs for students of all majors; the gallery is public weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.
cards.source_title: The Masters Mineral Gallery | Elizabethtown College
cards.access_notes: The gallery is open to the public from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays and is located in the Masters Center lobby.

cards.title: Work Through Problems in the Math Hideaway
cards.subtitle: The mathematics student lounge in Esbenshade E383
cards.notes: Use the departmental lounge for mathematics work, or shift to the nearby third-floor seating area when a whiteboard would help your group.
cards.short_summary: A named mathematics lounge paired with nearby seating and a whiteboard for collaborative problem-solving.
cards.evidence_claim: Elizabethtown College identifies the Mathematics Student Hideaway in E383 as a lounge for mathematics students and notes nearby third-floor seating with a whiteboard.
cards.access_notes: Located in the mathematics department office in Esbenshade E383 and intended for mathematics students; follow departmental and building-access rules.

cards.title: Study Near Psychology Faculty and Lab Resources
cards.subtitle: Second-floor commons in Esbenshade Hall
cards.notes: Use the commons seating for psychology or neuroscience work and consult nearby faculty when questions arise; verify lab availability separately.
cards.short_summary: A departmental gathering space connecting psychology students with faculty offices and an associated computer lab.
cards.evidence_claim: The College says the Psychology Commons houses faculty offices and the Psychology Computer Lab, with the lab serving as a frequent gathering place for psychology students.
cards.source_title: Psychology Labs and Facilities | Elizabethtown College
cards.access_notes: Located on Esbenshade Hall’s second floor. Computer-lab use depends on class scheduling and departmental access; academic buildings are not public-access buildings.
